resources.string: The diaphragm contracts and descends. Chest volume increases, lowering alveolar pressure below outside pressure so air enters.
Air passes through the bronchi and smaller bronchioles into the alveoli. Capillaries wrap around each air sac.
Two gases move in opposite directions
Across the alveolar lining, shared basement layer and capillary lining, O₂ diffuses toward blood and CO₂ toward air, each down its own partial-pressure gradient.
Red blood cells pick up oxygen as they flow through capillaries. Oxygen-rich blood returns to the left side of the heart through pulmonary veins.
The lungs recoil and air flows out
During quiet exhalation, the diaphragm relaxes and rises. The lungs recoil, and exhaled air carries carbon dioxide out. Gas exchange does not stop between breaths.
Ventilation, diffusion, and blood flow are shown in slow motion. Particle counts, image scale, and timing are illustrative, not measurements.
